cues: Four spelling rules that actually pay.
I before e, except after c, when the sound is ee: believe and field, but receive and ceiling, with exceptions like seize and weird.
Double the final consonant when the last syllable is stressed: stop, stopping; begin, beginning; but enter, entering.
Drop a silent e before a vowel suffix: hope, hoping, but hopeful; and notice keeps its e in noticeable, to protect the soft c.
And y becomes i after a consonant: happy, happiness; but play, played.
Two small ones: the suffix ful has one l, and all, well and till drop a letter in always, welcome and until.
